title: Araghchi: In wars, the environment is a silent victim
text:
Araghchi: In wars, the environment is a silent victim"

"Foreign Minister:"

"· The environmental situation in the Persian Gulf has been facing environmental disasters for years. The war that the United States launched in Iraq, the oil wells set ablaze, and the fires that broke out in the region all caused widespread damage to the environment of this region."

"· After that, too, because of the continuation of wars in this region, we have constantly faced the environmental consequences of these conflicts. Judging by what can be inferred from US policies, it seems this trend will continue."
"· The reality is that in wars, the environment is a silent victim. Nature, as a neutral element in war, perhaps suffers the greatest damage—damage whose effects are lasting and long-term."

"· In this recent war and aggression against Iran, we also witnessed how much damage was inflicted on the environment, people’s living environment, and their health. For example, in Tehran, when refinery storage tanks were targeted and a fire broke out, the city’s sky was dark for a full day and even two or three days, and black rain fell.
